note: The words the open world's townspeople say to the heir (the `talk` catalog; core/game/game_talk.gd and data/world/talk.json say when and which). A key is either a single line or a group of variants numbered from 1 (job.<job>.day.1, job.<job>.night.1, call.<job>.1, creature.<kind>.1, weather.<id>.1, standing.<rank>.1 ...). Placeholders: {heir}, {house}, {town}, {faction}, {gate}, {dest}, {creature}, {dir}, {paces}, {job}, {text}. Every line may be translated (data/text/locales/<id>/talk.json) with exactly the same placeholders.

lines.job.farmer.day.1: The barley wants cutting before the weather turns. Mind the furrows.
lines.job.farmer.day.2: A good field forgives a lot, traveller, but not a lazy man.
lines.job.farmer.night.1: No one should be afield at this hour. The owls keep the barley now.
lines.job.farmer.night.2: I sleep with one ear on the barn door. Foxes.
lines.call.farmer.1: Ho there, {heir}! Fine day for walking.
lines.call.farmer.2: Well met! Careful of the furrows.
lines.job.guard.day.1: I walk the streets so you can sleep in them. Keep your blade sheathed.
lines.job.guard.day.2: Quiet watch so far. I like it quiet.
lines.job.guard.night.1: The night round is the long one. Keep to the lamplit streets.
lines.job.guard.night.2: If you hear a bell, get indoors and bar the door.
lines.call.guard.1: Halt a moment, {heir}. The watch is looking at you, kindly.
lines.call.guard.2: Evening, traveller. Keep to the lit streets.
lines.job.smith_hand.day.1: I pump the bellows and the master does the pretty work. Mind the sparks.
lines.job.smith_hand.day.2: Iron does not care who your grandfather was. Pay in coin.
lines.job.smith_hand.night.1: The forge never goes cold, but I do. Home for me soon.
lines.job.smith_hand.night.2: Heard the hammer at midnight? That is the master, not a ghost.
lines.call.smith_hand.2: Need a blade mended? The forge is open.
lines.job.shop_hand.day.1: Everything is fair priced. Ask the storekeeper if you think otherwise.
lines.job.shop_hand.day.2: I count the crates and the crates count me. Busy day.
lines.job.shop_hand.night.1: We shut at dusk, but the lamps stay lit for a kind face.
lines.job.shop_hand.night.2: Stock is counted twice at night. Dull work, honest wages.
lines.call.shop_hand.1: Good day, {heir}! Fresh stock on the shelves.
lines.call.shop_hand.2: Step in, step in. No one regrets a look.
lines.job.tavern_hand.day.1: The ale is cold and the stew is hot. The reverse is cheaper.
lines.job.tavern_hand.day.2: Marta says never to listen to the regulars, so I only listen very carefully.
lines.job.tavern_hand.night.1: Busy night. Everyone has a story and no one has a coin.
lines.job.tavern_hand.night.2: Last orders soon. Or never, if the singing carries on.
lines.call.tavern_hand.1: Thirsty, traveller? The tavern has beds too.
lines.call.tavern_hand.2: Hello, {heir}! There is a fire inside.
lines.job.acolyte.day.1: Mind the candles. The sisters count them, and so do I.
lines.job.acolyte.day.2: A prayer costs nothing. The healing costs a little. That is only fair.
lines.job.acolyte.night.1: The night vigil is mine. Peaceful, if you ignore the draughts.
lines.job.acolyte.night.2: Quietly, please. The temple sleeps lightly.
lines.call.acolyte.2: The temple door is open to the weary.
lines.job.runner.day.1: I carry things from there to here and ask nothing. That is the job.
lines.job.runner.day.2: Nobody follows me. Nobody asks. Good, that.
lines.job.runner.night.1: Night is when business gets honest. Or at least quiet.
lines.job.runner.night.2: Lantern's not lit for a reason. Pass on.
lines.job.homekeeper.day.1: Someone has to keep the hearth lit and the roof on. That is me.
lines.job.homekeeper.day.2: The house has a lot of corners and every one of them needs dusting.
lines.job.homekeeper.night.1: The fire is banked and the doors are barred. Good night to you.
lines.job.homekeeper.night.2: Is it not late for walking about?
lines.call.homekeeper.2: Hello there! Keep to the street, the cat is nervous.
lines.job.gate_guard.day.1: Keep your weapons sheathed in town and your coin out of sight. That is all the law I need.
lines.job.gate_guard.day.2: A quiet gate is a good gate. Do not spoil it.
lines.job.gate_guard.night.1: Gate is shut to carts after dark but walkers may pass, lamp in hand.
lines.job.gate_guard.night.2: Night shift. If you are coming in, come in. If not, stop loitering.
lines.job.forge.day.1: Iron, steel and patience. Bring me ore and I will bring you edge.
lines.job.forge.day.2: Metal or mending? Say it quick, the fire is hungry.
lines.job.forge.night.1: The forge is banked, but I can still hear a good steel sing.
lines.job.forge.night.2: Late for a smith's visit, but the anvil does not mind.
lines.job.temple.day.1: The temple is open to the weary. Take your rest and your blessing.
lines.job.temple.day.2: Faith is a long road. Healing is a short one.
lines.job.temple.night.1: The vigil is long and the candles are short. Peace be with you.
lines.job.temple.night.2: Few come at night, and those who do need us most.
lines.job.store.day.1: Take your time. Everything on the shelf is honest weight.
lines.job.store.day.2: Looking for something particular, or just the warmth?
lines.job.store.night.1: We are nearly shut, but a good customer is a good customer.
lines.job.store.night.2: Late shopping, eh? I do not mind.
lines.call.store.2: Good day to you! The store is open.
lines.job.tavern.day.1: Sit, drink, tell me your news. The roads send me all sorts.
lines.job.tavern.day.2: A bed, a bowl and a seat by the fire. That is what I sell.
lines.job.tavern.night.1: Busy night, and the singing has not even started.
lines.job.tavern.night.2: Grab a seat before the regulars take them all.
lines.call.tavern.1: Welcome, {heir}! A seat by the fire?
lines.job.black_market.day.1: Quiet prices, quiet deals. You did not see the door.
lines.job.black_market.day.2: I sell what the store cannot. Do not ask where it comes from.
lines.job.black_market.night.1: Night is when my trade is honest. Lower your voice.
lines.job.black_market.night.2: Not many come at this hour. The ones who do are serious.
lines.creature.goblin.1: Heh. You are tall. We keep to the back houses, mostly.
lines.creature.goblin.2: Do not stare. We pay our rent in coin like everyone else.
lines.creature.ogre.1: Hrm. Door is small. Everything is small.
lines.creature.ogre.2: I do not smash things. Much. Mind the doorway.
lines.asleep.2: (mumbles something about the harvest and rolls over)
lines.asleep.3: (sound asleep, and not to be woken)
lines.weather.clear.2: Not a cloud. A rare thing.
lines.weather.overcast.1: The sky is gloomy. It may rain.
lines.weather.overcast.2: Grey as a sword. It could turn.
lines.weather.rain.1: Rain again. The roofs will tell.
lines.weather.rain.2: It pours. The boots will not dry.
lines.weather.storm.1: A storm is up. Shutters closed, if you ask me.
lines.weather.storm.2: Thunder in the hills. Do not stand under trees.
lines.weather.fog.1: Fog everywhere. You could walk into a wall.
lines.weather.fog.2: I cannot see my own feet in this fog.
lines.weather.heat.1: The heat is fierce. Drink often.
lines.weather.heat.2: Hot as an oven out here.
lines.weather.snow.1: Snow already! The roofs will be heavy.
lines.weather.snow.2: Cold enough to freeze the pump.
lines.standing.hostile.1: The {faction} do not forget how House {house} has behaved. Nor do I.
lines.standing.hostile.2: Mind your step, {heir}. The {faction} have you down as trouble.
lines.standing.wary.1: The {faction} watch your family closely. So do I.
lines.standing.wary.2: House {house} is not trusted here, not yet.
lines.standing.neutral.1: I know little of House {house}, and the {faction} know no more.
lines.standing.neutral.2: The {faction} have no quarrel with you. That is a start.
lines.standing.trusted.1: House {house} is well spoken of by the {faction}. That counts.
lines.standing.trusted.2: The {faction} trust your family, {heir}. So will we, with time.
lines.standing.honoured.1: House {house}! The {faction} honour your family. It is an honour for me, too.
lines.standing.honoured.2: Everyone knows what House {house} has done for the {faction}. Welcome.
lines.house.built.1: I hear House {house} has raised a house of its own outside the town. Good, to see roots.
lines.house.built.2: They say your family has built something. People who build, stay.
lines.house.none.1: Will House {house} be building a place of its own here someday?
lines.house.none.2: A family with no house of its own is just travellers. Build something.
lines.size.small.1: Being small, I know every low door and every cat in town.
lines.size.small.2: The big folk never notice me. It suits me.
lines.size.large.1: Doors are a nuisance when you are built like me.
lines.size.large.2: Everyone is smaller than I expected. Mind my elbows.
lines.size.heir_tall.1: You are a tall one, {heir}. Duck under the signs.
lines.size.heir_tall.2: A fair height on you. Do you eat well?
lines.size.heir_short.1: You are no giant, {heir}, but that is no fault.
lines.size.heir_short.2: Small folk get through crowds faster. You do well.
lines.race.human: Folk are folk, whatever you call them.
lines.race.halfling: Halflings like a good meal and a short walk. I am a fine example.
lines.race.elf: Years are long for my people. A day in the town barely counts.
lines.race.half_elf: Not quite one thing or the other. I have grown used to it.
lines.race.dwarf: Stone and steel, that is my people. Good stuff, both.
lines.race.gnome: Gnomes are curious. I will be asking you questions, so I hope you do not mind.
lines.race.half_orc: Some stare at the tusks. I stare back until they look away.
lines.race.orc: Orcs have a poor name, mostly from men who started it.
lines.race.beastkin: My ears hear what yours cannot. The wind talks, you know.
lines.race.half_dragon: Scales are warm in winter. I do not complain.
lines.race.dragonborn: My kind keeps our word. Remember that when we bargain.
lines.town.hearthmere.1: Hearthmere is a good place. Smoke, bells and gossip.
lines.town.hearthmere.2: The market in Hearthmere never sleeps for long.
lines.town.kingshold.1: Kingshold has a long memory and a longer tax list.
lines.town.kingshold.2: The noble houses look down on everyone in Kingshold, even each other.
lines.town.brinehaven.1: Brinehaven smells of salt and secrets, in that order.
lines.town.brinehaven.2: The tide brings everything to Brinehaven. Some of it should be thrown back.
lines.town.ironford.1: Ironford rings all day with hammers. You stop noticing.
lines.town.ironford.2: Dwarves founded Ironford and have never let us forget.
lines.gate.call.1: Halt a moment, {heir}. This is the {gate} of {town}; the road beyond leads to {dest}.
lines.gate.call.2: Welcome to {town}, traveller. You stand at the {gate}. The road runs on to {dest}.
lines.gate.call_plain.1: Halt a moment, {heir}. This is the {gate} of {town}. Keep your blade sheathed.
lines.gate.call_plain.2: Welcome to {town}, traveller. You stand at the {gate}.
lines.rumour.1: Folk say a {creature} was seen about {paces} paces {dir} of the town. Take care out there.
lines.rumour.2: A {creature} has been spotted some {paces} paces {dir} of here, they say.
lines.rumour.none.1: Nothing worth telling lately. The roads are quiet.
lines.rumour.none.2: No tales today. That is the best news.
lines.warn.1: Keep an eye out: a {creature} was seen about {paces} paces {dir} of the town.
lines.warn.2: A {creature} prowls some {paces} paces {dir} of the wall. Do not wander there unarmed.
lines.warn.none.1: Nothing near the town that I know of. Stay alert anyway.
lines.warn.none.2: All quiet beyond the wall, by my last look.
lines.wares.forge: The forge mends and sharpens, and makes steel for those who bring metal.
lines.wares.temple: The temple heals the hurt and sells blessings, at an honest price.
lines.wares.store: The store has potions, rope and travelling goods. Ask the storekeeper.
lines.wares.tavern: The tavern has food, a bed and sellswords seeking work, if you can pay.
lines.wares.black_market: Quiet goods at quiet prices. Do not ask how they were come by.
